messages.content: How do I add short-term memory (conversation history) to a LangGraph graph?

outputs.reference_answer: Compile the graph with a checkpointer, e.g. builder.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver()) for development or a Postgres checkpointer in production, and pass a thread id on every call: config={'configurable': {'thread_id': '...'}}. State, including messages, is saved per thread and reloaded on the next call. On LangSmith Deployments the platform supplies the checkpointer, so you don't pass one.

messages.content: How do I run an offline evaluation of my app against a LangSmith dataset in Python?

outputs.reference_answer: Create a dataset of examples (client.create_dataset and client.create_examples, or in the UI), write a target function that takes an example's inputs and returns outputs, write evaluators (functions over inputs/outputs/reference_outputs that return a score, or LLM-as-judge evaluators such as openevals), then call langsmith's evaluate(target, data='<dataset>', evaluators=[...], experiment_prefix='...'). Each run becomes an experiment on the dataset that you can compare in the UI.

messages.content: In an agent-based LangSmith workspace, how do I send my traces to a specific agent and environment?

outputs.reference_answer: Set LANGSMITH_AGENT_ID (the agent identifier, not its display name) and LANGSMITH_AGENT_ENVIRONMENT (local, development, staging or production) alongside LANGSMITH_TRACING and LANGSMITH_API_KEY, or pass address=ls.agent_address('<id>', '<env>') to @traceable or tracing_context. Needs langsmith>=0.14.9 in Python. Don't also set LANGSMITH_PROJECT: an agent and a project together are not allowed, and the SDK won't trace.

messages.content: How do I route my LangChain model calls through the LangSmith LLM Gateway?

outputs.reference_answer: Set LANGSMITH_GATEWAY=true (or a regional gateway URL) and use a workspace-scoped LangSmith API key with the gateway:invoke permission (LANGSMITH_API_KEY, or LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY as an override). Supported chat models such as ChatOpenAI and ChatAnthropic, and deep agents, then send requests to gateway.smith.langchain.com instead of the provider. Any OpenAI-compatible client can also call https://gateway.smith.langchain.com/v1 with a provider-prefixed model id. Gateway calls are traced to the 'gateway' project with tokens and cost.

create_deep_agent(model=None, tools=None, *, system_prompt, middleware, subagents, skills, memory, permissions, backend, interrupt_on, response_format, state_schema, context_schema, checkpointer, store, debug, name, cache). model and tools are positional; everything else is keyword-only. It returns a compiled LangGraph graph.

messages.content: What's the import path for init_chat_model and what are its main parameters?

outputs.reference_answer: from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model. Signature: init_chat_model(model=None, *, model_provider=None, configurable_fields=None, config_prefix=None, **kwargs). model can be 'provider:model' (e.g. 'openai:gpt-5.5') or a bare name whose provider is inferred; other kwargs such as temperature, max_tokens or base_url go to the provider's chat model class.

messages.content: In the deepagents source code, where does create_deep_agent assemble the main agent's middleware stack, and which built-in middleware run before middleware I pass in?

outputs.reference_answer: In libs/deepagents/deepagents/graph.py inside create_deep_agent. The stack starts with FilesystemMiddleware, then SubAgentMiddleware (when there are subagents), an internal parent-notifier middleware, the summarization middleware and PatchToolCallsMiddleware (plus AsyncSubAgentMiddleware if configured). User middleware is spliced in after that core, ahead of profile extras, SkillsMiddleware, prompt caching, MemoryMiddleware, HumanInTheLoopMiddleware and UnsupportedContentMiddleware.

messages.content: How does LangChain's init_chat_model figure out the provider when I pass a bare model name like 'gpt-5.5' with no prefix? Show me where in the source.

outputs.reference_answer: A helper, _attempt_infer_model_provider in langchain/chat_models/base.py (libs/langchain_v1 in the langchain repo), lowercases the name and matches prefixes: gpt-, o1, o3, chatgpt or text-davinci map to openai; claude to anthropic; command to cohere; gemini to Google (currently google_vertexai, with a warning). If nothing matches, init_chat_model raises an error asking for model_provider.

messages.content: Is this still correct for current LangChain? `from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor, create_tool_calling_agent`

outputs.reference_answer: No. In LangChain 1.x, langchain.agents no longer exports AgentExecutor or create_tool_calling_agent (the legacy agents live in langchain-classic). Use the new API: from langchain.agents import create_agent; agent = create_agent(model, tools=[...], system_prompt=...); agent.invoke({'messages': [...]}).

messages.content: Write a minimal Python example of a deep agent with one custom tool, and make sure the imports are right.

outputs.reference_answer: from deepagents import create_deep_agent, plus a plain Python function (or a langchain_core.tools @tool) as the tool; agent = create_deep_agent(model='openai:gpt-5.5', tools=[my_tool], system_prompt='...'); then agent.invoke({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': '...'}]}). The imports should be checked against the installed deepagents package.
